main_text.p: non defertur:vel quoniam sensus communis aliorum omnium princeps & causa præcipua, qui in medio cerebri ventriculo consistit, aut deletus est omninò, aut impeditus. At verò animalis spiritus per epilepsiæ insultus haud quaquam in cerebro supprimitur aut retinetur, sed uberius in cuncta membra duci propelliq; videtur, quemadmodum ex eo motu, quantumuis depravato, qui tum ipsis euenit epilepticis, unicuique licet percipere. His adde quòd non alius est spiritus motui, & alius sensui destinatus, sed unus utriusq; facultatis communis. Quòd igitur epileptici suis paroxysmis nihil omninò sentiant, animalem spiritum causari non oportet, sed sensum communem (sine quo alij nò sentiunt) qui tamen non prorsus est deletus, sed duntaxat morbo impeditus. Nam si omni ex parte deletus esset, profectò non viveret animal:quandoquidem haud quaquam sentiret. At animal, sensu definitur, teste philosophoCap.4., lib. de Partibus animalium, & earum causis. Propterea vitæ animalis sensus est perpetuus comes: sed ob nimiam cerebri conquassationem, compressionemq;, quæ epilepticorum paroxysmis fieri contingit,

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "quantumuis depravato" (the printed line break after "depraua" shows no hyphen, so the word is written whole); "consistit" (line end "con" with no visible hyphen); "par te" written as "parte" for the same reason. "Quòd" carries the grave accent as printed. "Quod" and "Quòd" are kept as they appear. Printed "s" in the body is written as plain s. The running head is taken as printed. The marginal note "Cap.4.," is shown as printed; its exact punctuation is uncertain.
